About this demo

Every route and preference calculation uses Brisbane City Council data. The base map is supplied by OpenStreetMap for display only and is never read by the routing algorithm.

Routes connect shared vertices in BCC Bikeway sections and the LGIP Existing Bikeway dataset. No missing connection is drawn. This planning graph does not contain current closures, legal direction or turning restrictions and is not a turn-by-turn navigation service.

Arrivals are nearby BCC cycleway nodes, not building entrances. Three preference modes can select the same path when the data favours it.

Protected bikeways uses mapped off-road length as a proxy; physical barriers are not verified. Traffic is a saved BCC signal-flow snapshot from 15 Sep 2026, not live traffic. Hills use terrain estimates from 2002 contours; bridge decks and tunnels are excluded. Check each route’s coverage.

Hazards are explicitly labelled sample scenarios or your local reports. They do not affect BCC route calculations. Ride movement is simulated; no GPS is used.

BCC Bikeway sections · BCC Existing Bikeway · BCC Intersection volume · BCC Intersection locations · BCC Contours 2002

AI Use Declaration

This application was developed with assistance from ChatGPT, Codex and Claude. The team reviewed, adapted and tested AI-assisted outputs before incorporating them into the project.

Coding work allocation

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Help me divide the coding work for our MVP into 5 parts, tasks should be separated equally and logistically.”

How it was used: Asked AI to suggest a logical allocation of coding responsibilities so that each team member could contribute fairly to the project.

Validation and incorporation: The suggested allocation informed our team’s development plan, grouping the MVP’s files and features into five areas of responsibility. This helped clarify each member’s tasks and balance the workload.

BCC Data presentation slide

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Here is the content for our BCC Data slide. Suggest me a simple visual layout of slide”

How it was used: Asked ChatGPT to suggest a visual layout for the BCC Data presentation slide using content provided by the team.

Validation and incorporation: The suggested layout was adapted for the BCC Data presentation slide. The team provided and checked all written content, technical information and data sources..

Presentation script editing

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “check my presentation script, fix the grammar and make any unclear wording sound more natural”

How it was used: Used to review the presentation script, correct grammatical errors and improve unclear or inappropriate word choices.

Validation and incorporation: The revised wording was used in the final presentation script. The original content and technical information were provided and checked by the team.

Git branch and merge guidance

Tool: ChatGPT

Example prompt: “Show me step by step how to create and switch branches, add and commit files, push my changes, and merge my work using Git.”

How it was used: Asked for step-by-step guidance on using Git, including creating and switching branches, adding and committing files, pushing changes and merging team members’ work.

Validation and incorporation: The guidance was used to manage individual Git branches and integrate the prototype files. Team members executed the commands and checked the repository after each operation.

Leaflet map troubleshooting

Tool: ChatGPT/ Codex

Example prompt: “The Leaflet map is not displaying correctly. Here are the relevant HTML and JavaScript files and a screenshot of the problem. Help me identify the possible causes and suggest how to test them.”

How it was used: Used to help diagnose technical problems in the prototype. The team provided relevant code, screenshots and error information, such as when the Leaflet map was not displaying correctly.

Validation and incorporation: The suggested troubleshooting steps were used to identify possible causes and test solutions. The team selected and applied the relevant fixes, then checked that the map and related interactions worked correctly.

BCC data processing and route calculation

Tool: ChatGPT / Codex

Example prompt: “Using these BCC bikeway datasets, help us process the data into a connected cycling network and calculate route options based on distance and route preferences.”

How it was used: AI assisted with designing and implementing the workflow that processes BCC bikeway data into a connected network and calculates route options. We provided the selected datasets, route requirements and expected behaviours.

Validation and incorporation: The output was adapted into the data-processing scripts and route calculation module. We reviewed the code, tested the routes on the map, corrected unrealistic connections and verified that the results matched our project requirements and data limitations.

WIP feedback transcription

Tool: Chat GPT

How it was used: Generative AI was used to transcribe an audio recording of the feedback received during the WIP demonstration. I reviewed the transcript against the recording, corrected clear transcription errors, and organised the feedback into key issues and further details.

Validation and incorporation: The transcript was used to summarise the WIP feedback and plan future improvements to the prototype. The team reviewed the AI output before using it in the feedback document.

Route preference and JavaScript implementation

Tool: Claude

Example prompt: “Could you add a route preference option to the existing MVP so users can filter routes? Also, organise the JS code and tell me why you selected it.”

How it was used: Used AI to help solve technical issues, mainly in coding, particularly when implementing and debugging interface functionality in JavaScript.

Validation and incorporation: AI-generated code and implementation guidance were used to extend the existing MVP. including route preference filtering and JavaScript interface interactions. The suggested file structure also informed how we organised the code across the five team roles.

Locating the destination-selection code

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Which part of the project controls the destination selection, and which file should I modify?”

How it was used: Asked for guidance on locating the code responsible for destination selection and understanding which files needed to be modified.

Validation and incorporation: The guidance was used to identify the relevant planner code before making changes. The existing project structure and behaviour were checked before editing.

Improving the destination-selection interaction

Tool: Claude

Example prompt: “How can I change the destination selection so that the selected destination is highlighted, while the other destination options remain visible and can still be switched?”

How it was used: Asked for coding guidance to improve the destination selection interaction so that selecting one destination would highlight it without hiding the other available destinations.

Validation and incorporation: The suggested approach informed changes to the destination selection logic in the planner. The resulting interaction was run and tested in the prototype to confirm that users could switch destinations.

Interpreting the route-planning interface

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “What is the difference between the four route preferences, the Safety-focused, Quick and Scenic route options, and the ‘Same path’ result in our current prototype?”

How it was used: Asked for help interpreting the implemented route-planning interface and distinguishing route preferences, generated route options, and the “Same path” result.

Validation and incorporation: The explanation was used to check that the implemented interface and presentation accurately described the behaviour of the route-planning feature. No route calculation results were generated by ChatGPT.

Integrating the destination update with Git

Tool: Chat GPT / Codex

Example prompt: “How should I commit and push my destination-selection change to the team repository, and which modified file should I include?”

How it was used: Asked for guidance on integrating an individual code change using Git, including selecting the relevant modified file, writing a commit message, and pushing the change.

Validation and incorporation: The guidance supported the Git workflow used to integrate the destination interaction update into the team repository.

Debugging disappearing destination options

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Why do the other destination options disappear after I select one, and how can I keep them visible so the user can switch destinations?”

How it was used: Asked for help reviewing the destination selection code and identifying why destination options disappeared after a selection was made.

Validation and incorporation: The explanation was used to understand the existing selection behaviour and guide the modification. The final behaviour was verified manually in the website.

Hazard logo design

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Help me design logo’s for different types of hazards like potholes, debris, roadworks, traffic, slippery and blocked paths. Don’t make them look too similar to each other give each a unique design.”

How it was used: Asked ChatGPT to help design clear and unique logos for different types of cycling hazards, including potholes, debris, roadworks, traffic, slippery surfaces and blocked paths. It was instructed to make each logo visually distinct so users could quickly recognise the different hazards.

Hazard display and reporting code

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Help me create and improve the code for displaying hazards and allowing users to report new hazards.”

How it was used: Used to receive example JavaScript, HTML and CSS code, as well as guidance for connecting the hazard feature to the website

Validation and incorporation: The example code was reviewed, modified and integrated into the hazard section of the prototype. The team tested the feature and adjusted it to work with the rest of the website

Uploading hazard files with Git

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Show me how to add my hazard files to my Git branch, commit the changes and push them to the team repository.”

How it was used: Used to receive step-by-step guidance and explanations of Git commands.

Validation and incorporation: The guidance was followed to manage and upload the hazard-feature files through the individual branch. The team member performed the commands and checked the repository after pushing the changes.

Community section design guidance

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “How should I design the Community section so cyclists can share useful road and safety information clearly?”

How it was used: Asked for design guidance for the Community section of the prototype, including how users could share cycling information, view posts and interact with community content.

Validation and incorporation: The suggestions were used to refine the structure of the Community interface and organise the main functions. The final layout and interaction choices were reviewed and adjusted manually to fit the overall prototype.

Community posting warning

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “How can I clearly remind users not to create false or misleading community posts without making the message too aggressive?”

How it was used: Asked for help improving the Community posting interaction, particularly how to remind users not to submit false or misleading cycling information.

Validation and incorporation: The wording and presentation suggestions were used as references when designing the warning shown during the posting process. The final message and visual style were adjusted to match the rest of the interface.

Future Plan slide organisation

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Can you help me shorten the Future Plan content into a few clear key points for the slide while keeping the detailed explanation in my presentation script?”

How it was used: Asked for help organising and simplifying the Future Plan section of the final presentation.

Validation and incorporation: The suggestions were used to reduce the amount of text on the slide and highlight the main future development ideas. I reviewed and edited the wording so that it accurately reflected our team’s actual plans.

Community and Future Plan presentation script

Tool: Chat GPT

Example prompt: “Can you help refine these two parts of my script so they take around 1.5–2 minutes without removing the important points?”

How it was used: Asked for help refining the presentation script for my assigned sections, including the Community and Future Plan content, and adjusting the length to fit the presentation time.

Validation and incorporation: The revised wording was used as a reference for the final speaking script. I checked and edited the content myself to make sure it matched the final prototype, slides and my individual contribution.
